result.title: Can You Find the Edit When Nothing Looks Wrong? A Paired Benchmark for Text-Driven Image Manipulation Localization Beyond Semantic Abnormality
result.summary: Instruction-driven image editing can alter a photograph while keeping the result coherent with the scene. Existing benchmarks lack matched plausible and anomalous edits of the same target, making it difficult to measure how localization performance changes with semantic plausibility. We construct a paired benchmark by generating semantically plausible and anomalous replacements of the same target in each source photograph. Both edits use the same editor, language, and generation settings. We estimate a separate mask for each output and retain pairs with sufficient mask overlap, enabling direct comparison of localization performance under the two semantic conditions. The release contains 47,747 bilingual triplets from 6,500 photographs, spanning four editors, three source domains, and six intended violation types. Across nine public localizers, editor-averaged IoU is lower on plausible edits in 26 of 27 model-dataset comparisons. This gap persists under pixel-change controls and region-size analyses. These findings reveal a semantic-plausibility shortcut: localization often weakens when an edited result looks ordinary. The benchmark provides a controlled setting for measuring this gap and developing localizers that remain effective on plausible edits.

AI.brief_summary: 构建配对基准：对同一目标分别生成语义合理与语义异常的编辑（同一编辑器与设置），保留掩码充分重叠的配对，在 6,500 张照片上比较九种定位器，发现编辑结果「看起来正常」时定位 IoU 系统性下降。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「语义合理性捷径」与配对控制设计可能可供核查：模型是否依赖语义先验而忽略细粒度视觉证据，可作为 VLM 视觉证据使用与捷径诊断的评价参考；但领域属图像取证，与 LVR 状态生成无直接联系。
